ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, in the equilateral triangle $\triangle CDE$ with the vertex $D$ sliding along the side $AB$ of the equilateral triangle $\triangle ABC$, $DE$ intersects $BC$ at point $F$. When $AD:DB=3:4$, what is the value of $\frac{BF}{CF}$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Given that $AD:DB=3:4$,\\
we can assume $AD=3k$, $BD=4k$, hence $AB=AC=BC=7k$,\\
since $\triangle ABC$ and $\triangle CDE$ are equilateral,\\
$\angle A=\angle B=\angle CDE=60^\circ$,\\
and since $\angle A+\angle ACD=\angle CDF+\angle BDF$,\\
it follows that $\angle ACD=\angle BDF$,\\
thus $\triangle ACD \sim \triangle BDF$,\\
implying that $\frac{AC}{BD}=\frac{AD}{BF}$,\\
thus $\frac{7k}{4k}=\frac{3k}{BF}$,\\
hence $BF=\frac{12}{7}k$,\\
therefore $CF=BC−BF=7k−\frac{12}{7}k=\frac{37}{7}k$,\\
hence $\frac{BF}{CF}=\frac{\frac{12}{7}k}{\frac{37}{7}k}=\boxed{\frac{12}{37}}$.

raw_record.original_question: As shown in the figure, in the equilateral triangle $\triangle CDE$ with the vertex $D$ sliding along the side $AB$ of the equilateral triangle $\triangle ABC$, $DE$ intersects $BC$ at point $F$. When $AD:DB=3:4$, what is the value of $\frac{BF}{CF}$?
raw_record.answer: \textbf{Solution:} Given that $AD:DB=3:4$, we can assume $AD=3k$, $BD=4k$, hence $AB=AC=BC=7k$. Since $\triangle ABC$ and $\triangle CDE$ are equilateral, $\angle A=\angle B=\angle CDE=60^\circ$, and since $\angle A+\angle ACD=\angle CDF+\angle BDF$, it follows that $\angle ACD=\angle BDF$. Thus $\triangle ACD \sim \triangle BDF$, implying that $\frac{AC}{BD}=\frac{AD}{BF}$. Thus $\frac{7k}{4k}=\frac{3k}{BF}$, hence $BF=\frac{12}{7}k$. Therefore $CF=BC-BF=7k-\frac{12}{7}k=\frac{37}{7}k$, hence $\frac{BF}{CF}=\frac{\frac{12}{7}k}{\frac{37}{7}k}=\boxed{\frac{12}{37}}$.
raw_record.final_cot: Image description: In the figure, the large triangle ABC is an equilateral triangle, A is above, B is at the lower left, and C is at the lower right; D lies on side AB; D, F, E are on the same straight line, and segment DE passes downward through BC at F; B, F, C are collinear. The figure also connects D to C and E to C, forming the equilateral triangle CDE. Reasoning: From AD:DB=3:4, let AD=3k and DB=4k, then AB=7k. Since △ABC is an equilateral triangle, AC=BC=AB=7k, and ∠CAD=60°, ∠DBF=60°. Since △CDE is an equilateral triangle, ∠CDF=60°. At point D, DB is the opposite extension of DA, and DF lies inside ∠BDC, so ∠BDC=∠BDF+∠CDF. On the other hand, the exterior angle ∠BDC in △ACD is ∠CAD+∠ACD=60°+∠ACD. Therefore 60°+∠ACD=∠BDF+60°, giving ∠ACD=∠BDF. Thus △ACD and △BDF have two corresponding angles equal: ∠CAD=∠DBF=60°, ∠ACD=∠BDF, so △ACD∼△BDF. By corresponding sides, AC/BD=AD/BF, that is, 7k/4k=3k/BF, solving gives BF=12k/7. Also CF=BC−BF=7k−12k/7=37k/7, so BF/CF=(12k/7)/(37k/7)=12/37.
